questions.q: What are the six Snowflake pieces this project's plan identifies, in order?
options: Warehouse, stage, raw table, summary query, view, and one read-only role
Database, schema, dbt project, Airflow DAG, dashboard, and admin role
Warehouse, Snowpipe, external stage, fact table, dimension table, and masking policy
Stage, view, warehouse, role, Snowpipe, and resource monitor
questions.explain: The plan maps directly onto the requirement: compute (warehouse), a landing spot for the file (stage), the loaded data (raw table), the answer (summary query), a stable object for Power BI (view), and read-only access (role).

questions.q: Why does this project reuse Driftwood's existing DRIFTWOOD_ANALYTICS database instead of creating a new one?
options: There's no reason to stand up a second database for one more data domain — a new schema (SUPPORT) is enough to keep it separated
Snowflake only allows one database per account
A new database would be more expensive than a new schema
The VP of Support requires access to the billing database
questions.explain: Adding a schema keeps support data cleanly separated without the unnecessary overhead of a whole new database for a small project.

questions.q: Why is an XS (extra-small) warehouse the right size for this project, per the lesson's reasoning?
options: The entire workload is loading one CSV a day and running one summary query — matching compute size to actual workload is the point
XS warehouses are the only size Snowflake offers for free accounts
Larger warehouses cannot run COPY INTO statements
The VP of Support specifically requested the smallest possible warehouse
questions.explain: The capstone consistently right-sizes tools to the actual job — the same reasoning the Advanced capstone uses when choosing scheduled batch loads over Snowpipe.

questions.q: What does this plan deliberately leave out, at this stage?
options: A dbt transformation layer, an orchestrator for the load, and a second role for a second stakeholder
Any SQL at all
The raw table
The VP of Support as a stakeholder
questions.explain: With one stakeholder, one source, and one manual daily load, there's nothing yet for a transformation framework, orchestrator, or extra role to coordinate.

questions.q: Why plan and name all six objects before writing any CREATE statements?
options: So each later lesson fills in SQL against an existing plan instead of improvising names mid-build
Because Snowflake requires all object names to be registered in advance
Because the VP of Support must approve every object name individually
Naming objects first is required for Power BI to recognize them
questions.explain: Deciding names and structure up front avoids inconsistent or confusing object names appearing later in the build.
